text:
olivia: Hi benefits team  quick one. Child born via international surrogacy in India on 2026-05-02. We landed back in the US last week. Hospital gave a newborn record and the agency provided a parentage order, but CRBA/passport are pending. Can I add the child retroactive to DOB? Any special docs we need for surrogacy cases?
clara-peopleops: Congrats, olivia! :tada: Tagging @noah-benefits for the official list. Also fyi some states require a US court parentage order after return.
benefits-bot: Surrogacy intake guidance: https://hr.redwood.example/surrogacy (check international checklist). Standard processing SLA: 3-7 business days after complete docs.
noah-benefits: Congrats and welcome! Short answers: yes  you can request retroactive coverage to the birth date if you report the QLE within 30 days of the qualifying event (DOB or placement date, whichever applies). International surrogacy cases need a slightly expanded doc set for initial enrollment. For provisional enrollment we typically accept ANY TWO of the following, but one of them should establish parental legal status (court order/parentage document preferred):
- Foreign birth certificate or newborn hospital record (with certified translation if not English)
- Court-issued parentage order, parentage judgment, or home-country decree establishing you as the legal parent(s)
- Official embassy/consulate letter acknowledging the child's registration/entry (or CRBA when issued)
- Child passport or provisional travel document
- Agency placement letter + signed surrogacy contract
If you don't yet have a US court parentage order, upload the agency parentage order + hospital discharge + embassy acknowledgment. Our team will provisionally enroll the child subject to final legal documentation (US court order or CRBA/passport) when available. We do require final legal parentage proof once it's issued before enrollment is finalized.
olivia: Helpful, thanks. Do we need genetic testing or notarized affidavits? The agency mentioned a pre-birth parentage recognition letter.
noah-benefits: We don't require genetic testing as a rule. Notarized affidavits can help as supplemental evidence but aren't a substitute for a legal parentage order if that's what's required by state law. The usual path: provisional enrollment on agency docs + embassy letter/hospital record; then submit CRBA/passport or US parentage order when you have it.
payroll-bot: Payroll note: If coverage is made effective retro to 2026-05-02, premiums will be reconciled retroactively in the next 1-2 pay cycles after benefits processes the event. You might see a one-time deduction or a refund depending on previous withholdings. If timing is tight, payroll can split the adjustment across two runs if you request it (email payroll@redwood.example).
olivia: We don't have an SSN yet. Is that a blocker?
noah-benefits: SSN is not required to add the dependent initially. Provide SSN within 60 days when it's issued; if not provided we will follow up. For tax-advantaged accounts (FSA/HSA) keep payroll informed if plan choice changes.
clara-peopleops: Where do I upload the docs for surrogacy intake? I tried "Report a life event" but wasn't sure which event to pick.
noah-benefits: Steps: HR Portal > Benefits > Report a Life Event > Select: "Add dependent  qualified life event (newborn/placement)" > Enter DOB/placement date: 2026-05-02 > Relationship: child > Upload all files (you can attach multiple PDFs) > In notes put: "International surrogacy  agency parentage order + hospital record attached; CRBA/passport pending; will upload US parentage order when available" Alternatively open a case and attach docs and cc benefits@redwood.example.
benefits-bot: Example note to paste: "Newborn via international surrogacy. DOB: 2026-05-02. Attached: hospital newborn record, agency parentage order, embassy registration letter pending CRBA. Requesting provisional enrollment retro to DOB."
olivia: Thanks  uploading agency + hospital records now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.
noah-benefits: Case created: #SUR-33455. We'll review and aim to respond within 3-5 business days. If we need the US court order or CRBA later we'll ping you here.
clara-peopleops: Huge congrats again  ping if you want someone to help with the portal upload.
